messages:
meera: Customer escalation: multiple 502s and timeouts on /v1/generate around 17:52 UTC. p95 jumped to ~8s. Customer supplied req ids: req-A13, req-A14. They're replaying long transcripts after a local failure and rate limit didn't stop the burst. Please triage.

jem: Dashboard shows request_queue_depth spike to ~19k at 17:51. Alert fired: gateway.queued_depth>8000. p95 correlates.

ops-bot: automated detection: continuous-batcher backlog growing on pool hosted-prod-us-east-2. KV-cache miss rate increased ~5.8x. Sample trace t-8c9d indicates >9k queued tokens.

sam: hypothesis: a flood of long streaming requests monopolizing KV slots and preventing batch flush -> head-of-line backlog. Suggest grep logs for seq_len>30000 and state=streaming.

tony: confirmed 42 concurrent streaming requests with seq_len >= 30k during the spike. Example log:
```
[17:50:01] req=req-A13 sess=s-ff12 state=streaming seq_len=34820 pool=hosted-prod-us-east-2
[17:50:10] queue_size=19012 batch_window_ms=45 kv_cache_bytes=845MiB
```

meera: customer admits they retried a large set of transcripts after a crash. They expected client-side retries to be throttled but traffic came in as a short burst.

jem: short-term mitigations: (a) per-tenant ingress throttle, (b) reduce continuous_batcher.window_ms to force more frequent flush, (c) route very-long requests to a separate slow-path pool. Thoughts?

sam: do (a) and (b) now. I'll flip a per-tenant throttle for org-987 (drop to 30% of peak) and reduce window_ms 45->12ms for hosted-prod-us-east-2. Note: CPU and token-rate will rise slightly.

tony: I'll add a runtime route for requests with seq_len>16k to hosted-slow-2 (separate autoscale, smaller batch windows, isolated KV cache) to avoid head-of-line blocking.

meera: customer notified: "Temporary throttle + routing to a separate pool applied. You may see degraded success for very-long streaming requests for ~30m." They acknowledged and asked for repro guidance.

sam: internal repro steps for runbook:
- run loadgen: 120 streaming requests with seq_len=32k over 90s
- observe queue_depth and continuous_batcher.backlog_seconds
- expected: p95 >5s and some 502s when queue_depth >8k
- log checks: filter for `state=streaming` and seq_len>16000

jem: throttle applied at 17:58 UTC (org-987) -> ingress rate down ~70%. window_ms set to 12ms at 17:59. queue dropped from 19k -> ~2.5k by 18:06.

ops-bot: metrics snapshot post-mitigation:
- peak queue_depth 19,012 @17:51
- kv_cache_miss_rate up 5.8x during spike
- continuous_batcher.backlog_seconds avg 39s -> 5s after changes

tony: route deployed at 18:04; hosted-slow-2 is handling seq_len>16k requests with lower concurrency and independent autoscaler.

meera: customer reports fewer 502s at 18:12 and provided support logs. They requested a PM: default per-request soft cap for streaming seq_len or stronger server-side rate-limits to avoid accidental replays.

sam: follow-ups:
- sam: draft throttle/runbook docs and rollback steps (ETA 1h)
- tony: implement auto-detection for mass long-request replays per-tenant and auto-throttle (ETA 48h)
- eng-sre: propose soft cap (e.g., 20k) with clear 429 and guidance (schedule planning)
- meera: send full timeline & mitigation summary to customer (done)

jem: incident mitigated. queue normalized by ~18:10. Monitoring on for 24h. Marking mitigated; follow-up required for prevention. :white_check_mark:

meera: tagging for postmortem: @sam @tony @jem. I'll draft a short retrospective and link runbook.
